hits.comment_text:
The problem is "remote" SQLite. Just run a "single" beefier box with in-process SQLite and Litestream backups to object storage and never have to think about RDBMS again. I'd wager there are 90%+ applications that would be better served, more performant, and cheaper with this design.

I'm able to handle around 200k/s on a sub $100 box. https://github.com/pairshaped/gleam_sqlite_benchmarks/blob/m...

hits.author: AgentME
hits.comment_text:
The comparisons between various projects, including between rqlite and Litestream, were interesting. (rqlite uses a consensus algorithm between nodes to keep them synced and allow changing the primary node, while Litestream just syncs itself to S3 so another node could take over with the data from there.)

I fully expected the article to get into D1 shortly and mention how that's about the same relationship between Cloudflare Durable Objects (which D1 is based on) and celld, an open source reimplementation of Cloudflare Durable Objects which writes to S3. But then the article treats D1 with a very sudden snarky disinterest, and then the final section feels very awkwardly defensive of rqlite and defeatist.

hits.author: gizzlon
hits.comment_text:
I've been looking for a reason to use rqlite, but so far sqlite + litestream have been safe enough (some dataloss acceptable in extreme cases)

My understanding is that rqlite gives you "stored in more than place" guarantees, which is nice if you need it. Much slower than a 1 node db though.

hits.author: tilemarch
hits.comment_text:
Same experience here, from a multiplayer game server. Go, one SQLite file per game world, one process owns each file, all on a local SSD.

In a load test with 512 players all active on one world, command acks were 4-6 ms at the median and under 50 ms at p95, on a single Ryzen 9 3900X box. And most of that time is game logic and fanning out updates over websockets, not the database.

The part people worry about is durability, because SSDs have limited write cycles. So I took care to have backups of the state, recovery in short time etc.

I stream the WAL to object storage with Litestream, with one gotcha: I had to turn off SQLite’s own auto-checkpoint and let only Litestream checkpoint, or the two step on each other.
